bio.en: Phyl Terry is the author of Never Search Alone and a veteran operator - he was on the founding team of the first company Amazon acquired and later ran the consulting firm Creative Good - who has reinvented job searching through peer support.
bio.zh: Phyl Terry 是《永远不要独自求职》（Never Search Alone）一书的作者，也是一位资深从业者——他曾是亚马逊收购的第一家公司的创始团队成员，后来运营咨询公司 Creative Good——他通过同伴互助重新发明了求职方式。

summary.en: Phyl argues that job searching should be done with others, not alone, and introduces Job Search Councils: free, volunteer-run support groups of six to eight seekers who meet weekly using a structured methodology. He explains the 'spear, not a net' approach to candidate-market fit and why treating the search like a product exercise reveals focus. The episode is a compassionate, tactical playbook for finding work you love.
summary.zh: Phyl 主张求职应当与他人同行，而非孤军奋战，并介绍了“求职委员会（Job Search Councils）”：由 6-8 名求职者组成、免费且由志愿者运营的互助小组，每周按结构化方法碰面。他阐释了用“长矛而非渔网”的思路去匹配“候选人—市场”契合度，以及为何把求职当作产品练习能让人聚焦。本期是一份充满同理心、可落地的“找到热爱的工作”实战手册。

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: When you're looking for a job, you need a spear and not a net. What happens when we're building a product? Same thing, right? We want this product to be for everyone, but we've learned with product market fit that doesn't work. We need a narrow, clear focus.
turns.zh: 当你在找工作的时候，你需要的是一支长矛，而不是一张网。我们打造产品时会发生什么？也是一样，对吧？我们希望这个产品是给所有人用的，但通过产品市场契合我们学到，那样行不通。我们需要一个狭窄、清晰的焦点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: How did you realize this is a really powerful method versus the way people normally look for jobs?
turns.zh: 你是怎么意识到这是一种比人们通常找工作的方式更强大的方法的？

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: While it's hard to figure out your candidate market fit, it's also a relief to know it's not about you. So what I ask people to do is I ask them to think about what they want and what they don't want. Now, you might not think that that's a radical step, Lenny, but most people don't do that. When they get laid off, they spray and pray.
turns.zh: 虽然搞清楚你的"候选人市场契合"（candidate market fit）很难，但知道这跟你无关也是一种解脱。所以我让人们做的是，我让他们想想自己想要什么、不想要什么。现在，你可能不觉得这是个激进的步骤，Lenny，但大多数人不会这么做。当他们被裁员时，他们会"广撒网、碰运气"（spray and pray）。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is very much like a product person thinks about new product.
turns.zh: 这非常像一个产品人思考新产品的方式。

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: There's no I in team. Well, there is an I in village, and the I in village is that when you start to interview and negotiate, you've got to be in charge. I want you to play to win, not not to lose.
turns.zh: 团队（team）里没有"I"（我）。但在村庄（village）里有"I"，而村庄里的"I"意味着，当你开始面试和谈判时，你必须掌控局面。我要你为赢而战，而不是为不输而战。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything else that you think might be helpful to people looking for jobs?
turns.zh: 对于找工作的人，你觉得还有什么可能有帮助的吗？

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: If someone did this, it would blow my mind. I would hire them on the spot.
turns.zh: 如果有人这么做，我会惊掉下巴。我会当场雇佣他们。

Phyl also co-authored Customers Included, has written articles for the Harvard Business Review, and has delivered more than 500 keynotes to companies like Apple and Microsoft. This episode is for anyone struggling to find a job or unhappy in the job that they're in. I promise you, the time you put into listening to this episode will help you find a job that you love. turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: Oh, what a pleasure. I'm such a fan of yours, Lenny.
turns.zh: 哦，太荣幸了。我是你的超级粉丝，Lenny。

turns.en: I'm thrilled to be here.
turns.zh: 我很高兴来到这里。

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: Thank you.

turns.speaker: Lenny

What I'm hoping that we can do in our chat today is to help people who are struggling to find a job and especially struggling to find a job they love, actually find that job with actual tips that they can use today in this week. turns.zh: 我是你的超级粉丝，而且我想聊完之后我会成为你更大的粉丝。我希望我们今天能帮到那些正在挣扎找工作、尤其是找不到自己热爱的工作的人，用他们这周就能用上的实际建议，真正找到那份工作。你觉得怎么样？

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: That's great. We have some practical time-tested stuff that I've developed over the last 25 years with leaders in Silicon Valley, especially in the product community. We've really brought a product lens to reinventing the job search, Lenny.
turns.zh: 太好了。我们有一些经过时间检验的实用方法，是过去 25 年我和硅谷的领导者们、尤其是产品圈一起打磨出来的。我们真的把产品的视角带进了求职的重塑，Lenny。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is a perfect Venn diagram of topics then.
turns.zh: 那这就是个完美的韦恩图（Venn diagram）话题了。

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's a lot of ways I can approach this. I want to start with a question about something that you run, something that you created, something that has had a lot of impact on a lot of people: Job Search Councils. What is a Job Search Council?
turns.zh: 我有很多切入方式。我想从一个关于你运营的东西的问题开始——你创建的一个对很多人产生了很大影响的东西：求职委员会（Job Search Councils）。什么是求职委员会？

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: It's a support group of six to eight job seekers, so product people, but it is not just for product people, but the product community really owns this, it comes out of the product community. And what they do is they commit to being with each other, to supporting each other, go through the process of looking for a job and I lay out a methodology, how to figure out your candidate market fit, one of the big concepts in the book. As well as how to play to win, not not to lose. You know what I mean? People are scared in the job search. Here's the thing, Lenny, that people really have a hard time believing, everyone, I mean everyone, and I work with some of the most senior people in Silicon Valley, I'm talking about CEOs of public companies, I'm talking about chief product officers, VPs of product at great brands, everyone, no matter who they are, Lenny, feels insecure and anxious in the job search. And if you do it alone, it magnifies that. (00:03:57): So with Job Search Councils, there's this great hack, I didn't invent this, it's baked into human psychology, if you put anxious people together and ask them to be open and vulnerable and to ask for help, and we'll come back to asking for help, it actually flips the anxiety and the fear into hope, into motivation, into accountability and confidence. It's like, "What [inaudible 00:04:20]?" It's fantastic. My mother taught me this, we can talk about her at some point, but it's really powerful.
turns.zh: 它是一个由六到八名求职者组成的小组，当然是产品人，但它不只给产品人，而是产品圈真正拥有它，它来自产品圈。他们做的是承诺彼此相伴、彼此支持，一起走过找工作的过程，而我给出一套方法论——怎么搞清楚你的"候选人市场契合"，这是书里一个核心概念。还有怎么"为赢而战，而不是为不输而战"。你懂我意思吗？人们在求职时很害怕。Lenny，人们真的很难相信这一点，每个人，我是说每个人，我和硅谷一些最高层的人一起工作——我说的是上市公司的 CEO、首席产品官、大品牌的产品副总裁——每个人，无论他们是谁，Lenny，在求职时都会感到不安全和焦虑。而如果你独自去做，这种感觉会被放大。(00:03:57)：所以求职委员会有个很棒的窍门，那不是我发明的，它根植于人类心理：如果你把焦虑的人聚到一起，让他们开放、脆弱、去寻求帮助（我们待会儿会回到"寻求帮助"上），它其实会把焦虑和恐惧转化为希望、转化为动力、转化为责任感与信心。就像"什么[听不清 00:04:20]？"太妙了。这是我妈妈教我的，我们以后可以聊她，但它真的很有力量。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's amazing. Your whole book is called Never Search Alone, so the whole premise of how you recommend people look for jobs is to look for jobs with other people. You mentioned maybe it's your mom, maybe it's something else, how did you realize this is a really powerful method versus the way people normally look for jobs?
turns.zh: 太了不起了。你的整本书叫《Never Search Alone》（永不独自求职），所以你推荐人们找工作的方式的核心前提，就是和别人一起找工作。你提到也许是你的妈妈、也许是别的什么，你是怎么意识到这是一种比人们通常找工作的方式更强大的方法的？

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: Yeah. I set up my first council more than four years ago. I set up the first CEO council for internet CEOs in the mid '90s, and then I've run product and CEO council since. But it goes all the way back to my mom. 1960, Lenny, 1960, what is that? 64 years ago? In the San Fernando Valley, my mom was a newly-minted elementary school teacher, and she put together a council of teachers. That group met for 50 years, 5-0, until the year she died. They worked together to ask for help and support each other in their careers. And Lenny, people say to me, "Does this Never Search Alone method work in a tough job market?" And I'll tell you, it comes out of tough job markets. Absolutely, yes. Starting with my mom. (00:05:39): So in 1974, my dad... in 1976 he left and it was just me and my mom and my sister. He had insisted that she stop teaching, so she lost her tenure and everything. Her candidate market fit was terrible, but she had her council. It was the mid '70s, and Lenny, you probably can't imagine how hard it was for a single middle-aged woman with kids looking for a job in Los Angeles in the mid '70s. It was terrible. But she had her support group and they held her hand. The job she could get, guess what? She had to be an entry level teacher again after having been a senior teacher coaching and advising. It was really tough. So that had a big impact on me. (00:06:22): And then when the dotcom bubble burst, I was running Creative Good, and suddenly there was a depression. And suddenly I'm helping hundreds of people try to figure out their job search. So it's been going for a number of years, but it goes back to my mom. I dedicate the book to her and the community we've built.
turns.zh: 对。我在四年多前建立了我的第一个委员会。我在 90 年代中期建立了第一个互联网 CEO 委员会，从那以后就一直在运营产品和 CEO 委员会。但它要一直追到我妈妈。1960 年，Lenny，1960 年，那是多久？64 年前？在圣费尔南多谷，我妈妈是个刚拿到资格的小学老师，她组建了一个教师委员会。那个小组聚会了 50 年，5-0，直到她去世那年。她们一起协作、寻求帮助、在职业上彼此支持。Lenny，人们会问我"这个永不独自求职的方法在艰难的就业市场管用吗？"我告诉你，它恰恰来自艰难的就业市场。绝对管用。从我妈妈开始。(00:05:39)：1974 年，我爸爸……1976 年他离开了，只剩下我、我妈和我妹妹。他曾坚持让她停止教书，所以她丢了 tenure（终身教职）和一切。她的候选人市场契合很糟，但她有她的委员会。那是 70 年代中期，Lenny，你大概无法想象一个带着孩子的中年单身女性在 70 年代中期的洛杉矶找工作有多难。太糟了。但她有她的支持小组，她们握着她的手。她能找到的工作是什么？猜猜——她曾是高年级老师、指导和顾问，却不得不再从头做起当个入门级老师。真的很难。所以这对我影响很大。(00:06:22)：然后互联网泡沫破灭时，我在运营 Creative Good，突然间陷入萧条。突然我就在帮几百个人想办法求职。所以这件事已经持续好些年了，但根源在我妈妈。我把这本书献给了她和我们所建立的社区。

turns.en: You said that it's free. I know these things aren't free to run.
turns.zh: 你说它是免费的。我知道这些事运营起来并不免费。

turns.speaker: Phyl Terry
turns.en: Yeah.

turns.zh: 我在某处看到你提到，基本上你所有的书售收入、还有你自己的钱，都花在运营这些委员会上。聊聊这个。

turns.en: Yeah, actually two times the book sales are going into running this.
